Description: Read the arrow from tail to tip. Both axes use one unit per tick. The arrow starts at (1,1) and ends at (4,3).
Length in two perpendicular directions. The arrow runs three units across and four units up. Its length is the straight-line distance between its endpoints.
Compare two directions. The rightward arrow ends at (2,0). The other ends at (−1,2). The angle between them exceeds a right angle.
Find an entry by its two indices. Rows are examples; columns are features. Counting starts at zero. The rows are [2,5,1] and [4,3,8]. Matrix rows are [[2, 5, 1], [4, 3, 8]].
Multiply matching coordinates. One sample has features [1,3]. For one output, their weights are [2,4]. There is no bias. Matrix rows are [[1, 2], [3, 4]].
Count independent directions after a map. The dashed outline is a unit square. Every point in the filled input square is mapped onto the horizontal line segment from (0,0) to (2,0).
Compare stretches of the two axes. A unit square aligned with the coordinate axes maps to a rectangle 3 units wide and 2 units tall, with no rotation.
Compare unit areas. The input square is one unit wide and tall. The output parallelogram has horizontal base 2 and perpendicular height 1.

Read a local sensitivity table. Rows correspond to outputs y₀ and y₁. Columns correspond to inputs x₀ and x₁. Entries give local output change per unit input change. Matrix rows are [[2, -1], [4, 3]].
Read slope as rise divided by run. One point on the straight line is (1,3) and another is (3,7).
Two curves share the same bottom. Both curves reach zero at the origin. At x=1, A has risen to 1 and B has risen to 4.

Choose the right group before dividing. The columns contain people who did or did not receive an alert. The counts are [9,1] in the positive row and [3,87] in the negative row. Matrix rows are [[9, 1], [3, 87]].
Same center, different spread. Group A contains 4, 5 and 6; group B contains 1, 5 and 9. Each dot represents one observation.
Combine a prior with one observation. The two states start equally likely. The observed clue is three times more likely in state A than in state B.
Read likelihood from a curve. The evidence is three successes and one failure in four independent trials. The curve shows how likely this sequence is at each possible success probability.
Outcome frequencies are unequal. A has probability one-half, B one-quarter, and C and D one-eighth each.
A mean gives each draw one vote. Four equally weighted samples give function values 1, 2, 2 and 7.
Read an uncertainty interval. The endpoints shown are −0.02 and +0.05; zero represents equal performance.
Choose a direction from a point cloud. The cloud extends from lower left to upper right, close to the line y=x, with little spread across that line.
Read a classifier boundary. The classifier predicts positive when feature 1 exceeds 2, regardless of feature 2. A=(1,3) and B=(3,1).
Assign a point to a center. On a number line the cluster centers sit at 1 and 8. The new observation lies at 6.
Read a downhill step. The loss is the parabola (x−2)². You start at x=0 and may move a small distance left or right.
Follow a sliding window. The signal is [2,4,1,3]. Each output adds two adjacent entries with stride one and no padding. Positions are numbered from zero. Matrix rows are [[2, 4, 1, 3]].
Read a single attention row. A row contains the weights for one query over three keys. The first row is [0.1,0.7,0.2], the second [0.6,0.1,0.3]. Matrix rows are [[0.1, 0.7, 0.2], [0.6, 0.1, 0.3]].
Read a velocity from two locations. At time 0 a sample sits at (1,2). At time 1 it sits at (4,4). The path is straight and speed is constant.
Trace a fixed compute budget. Each plotted pair has parameters × tokens = 24 in normalized units. The parameter counts shown are 2, 3, 4 and 6.
Read a pipeline schedule. One means busy and zero means idle. Each column is one clock tick, and each row represents a different stage. Matrix rows are [[1, 1, 1, 0], [0, 1, 1, 1]].
Read a chance branch. Taking one action has two possible outcomes. One pays 4 with probability ¼ and the other pays 0 with probability ¾.
Read old and new action probabilities. For the same state and sampled action, the old policy assigns 0.2 and the new policy assigns 0.3.
Read a relative reward. Two answers to the same prompt have scores 1 and 3. In this preference model, only the difference between scores matters.
Round onto a representable grid. The only representable values near this input are 0, 0.5 and 1. The original activation is 0.62. Use nearest-value rounding.
Distinguish answered from correct. A model answers 60 items correctly, answers 20 incorrectly and abstains on the other 20.

Compare a row and a column. The input column has shape [2,1]. A row has shape [1,3]. Broadcasting adds every row entry to every column entry. Matrix rows are [[2], [5]]. Matrix rows are [[10, 20, 30]].

Read a graph from its neighbor table. Rows and columns follow A, B, C, D. An entry of one means a direct undirected connection, and zero means there is no edge. Matrix rows are [[0, 1, 0, 0], [1, 0, 1, 0], [0, 1, 0, 1], [0, 0, 1, 0]].
Read the image of a basis vector. The columns of this matrix tell where the two coordinate arrows land. The first input arrow is (1,0). Matrix rows are [[2, -1], [3, 4]].
Follow two arrows head to tail. The first arrow goes from (0,0) to (2,1). The second begins there and ends at (1,4).
Check which arrow stays on its line. This map sends (1,0) to (2,0), and (1,1) to (2,3). An eigenvector is a nonzero vector whose image is a scalar multiple of itself.
Read a density as an area. A continuous variable is uniform from 0 to 4 with density 0.25 everywhere on that interval. Consider the part from 1 to 3.
Read how two variables move together. As the horizontal values rise from 1 to 5, the vertical values run 8, 7, 6, 3 and 2.
Turn nonnegative weights into probabilities. Exponentiating three logits produced weights 2, 1 and 1. These weights still need to be normalized.
Compare a model with the data source. The source gives A and B equal probability. Model X does the same. Model Y assigns A 0.9 and B 0.1. Matrix rows are [[0.5, 0.5], [0.5, 0.5], [0.9, 0.1]].
Find the average prediction error. The true value at this input is 5. Three equally likely training samples yield predictors with outputs 6, 7 and 8.

Compare prediction to target. The classifier assigns probability 0.2 to the correct class C. Its one-hot target for C is 1. Use the logit gradient p minus target. Matrix rows are [[0.3, 0.5, 0.2], [0.0, 0.0, 1.0]].
Read a forecast bin. Ten items have predicted probability 0.8. Exactly six of them turn out positive.
Center the features within one token. One token’s two feature values are 2 and 6. For this step, subtract their shared mean without dividing by a standard deviation.
Read a router assignment matrix. Each row is a token. An entry of 1 means that token uses the expert in that column. Expert indices begin at zero. Matrix rows are [[1, 0, 1], [0, 1, 1], [1, 0, 1]].
Put a future payoff in today’s units. You receive zero now and 8 exactly two discount steps from now. Each step multiplies the weight by 0.5.

Count successful candidate pairs. A pool contains one correct answer A and two incorrect answers B and C. Sample two distinct answers uniformly without replacement. Matrix rows are [[1, 1, 0], [1, 0, 1], [0, 1, 1]].
Read a quantization residual. An original scalar weight 1.3 is represented by 1.5 after rounding. Define error as reconstructed minus original.
Find a break-even point. Plan A starts at zero and costs 4 units per request. Plan B has an 8-unit up-front cost and costs 2 units per request.
